questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Logistic Growth Initial Value Problem
questions.problem:
The rate of growth of the bear population $P(t)$ in a certain forest follows the logistic growth model

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.2P(4\,500-P),
$$

where $t$ is the time, in years. Find an expression for the bear population after $t$ years, given that there were $150$ bears initially.
questions.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality is $k=0.2,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=4\,500.$ 

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{4\,500}{1+C{e}^{-(4\,500\cdot 0.2)t}}=\frac{4\,500}{1+C{e}^{-900t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=150$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4\,500}{1+C{e}^{-900\cdot 0}} & =150 \\ 1+C & =\frac{4\,500}{150} \\ C & =30-1 \\  & =29.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t)=\frac{4\,500}{1+29{e}^{-900t}}.
$$

Since the growth rate of infected fishes is *jointly* proportional to the number of fishes that have been infected at time $t,$ and the number that have not, the number of infected fishes follows a logistic growth model.

$$

$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality is $k=0.009,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=130.$ Therefore, the growth of the number of fishes with fungal infection is given by the equation

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.009P(130-P).
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{130}{1+C{e}^{-(130\cdot 0.009)t}}=\frac{130}{1+C{e}^{-1.17t}}.

\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}}.

$$

questions.problem:
The population $P(t)$ of rabbits on a particular island follows the logistic growth model

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.2P-0.0002{P}^{2},
$$

where $t$ is the time, measured in years. If there were $400$ rabbits on the island initially, how many rabbits inhabited the island after $3$ years? Round your answer to the nearest integer.

After $3$ years, approximately
{{field-1}} rabbits inhabited the island.
questions.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity. 

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}},
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

We start by factoring the given differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dP}{dt} & =0.2P-0.0002{P}^{2} \\  & =0.0002P(1000-P).\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that the constant of proportionality is $k=0.0002,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=1000.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
P(t)=\frac{1000}{1+C{e}^{-(1000\cdot 0.0002)t}}=\frac{1000}{1+C{e}^{-0.2t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=400$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1000}{1+C{e}^{-0.2(0)}} & =400 \\ 1+C & =\frac{1000}{400} \\ C & =2.5-1 \\  & =1.5.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t)=\frac{1000}{1+1.5{e}^{-0.2t}}.
$$

Finally, we substitute $t=3$ into the expression for $P(t),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(3) & =\frac{1000}{1+1.5{e}^{-0.2(3)}} \\  & ≈548.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, after $3$ years, approximately $548$ rabbits inhabited the island.

canonical_examples.problem:
The rate of growth of the panda population $P(t)$ in a particular forest follows the logistic growth model is

$$
\dfrac{\mathrm{d} P}{\mathrm{d} t} = 0.001\,25 P(800-P),
$$

where $t$ is the time, in years, since the beginning of the observations. Find an expression for the panda population after $t$ years, given that there were $400$ pandas initially.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\dfrac{\mathrm{d} P}{\mathrm{d} t} = kP(a-P),
$$

where $k > 0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a > P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t) = \dfrac{a}{1+Ce^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality is $k=0.001\,25,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=800.$ 

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
P(t) 
= \dfrac{800}{1+Ce^{-(800\cdot 0.001\,25)t}}= \dfrac{800}{1+Ce^{-t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=400$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{800}{1+C{e}^{-0}} & =400 \\ \frac{800}{1+C} & =400 \\ \frac{1+C}{800} & =\frac{1}{400} \\ 1+C & =\frac{800}{400} \\ C & =2-1 \\ C & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the panda population is given by

$$
P(t)= \dfrac{800}{1+e^{-t}} .
$$

canonical_examples.problem: The growth rate of the hare population $P(t)$ in a particular forest is jointly proportional to the hare population at time $t,$ measured in years, and the difference between the forest's carrying capacity and the hare population. canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Since the hare population's growth rate is *jointly* proportional to the hare population at time $t$ and the difference between the carrying capacity and the hare population, the hare population follows a logistic growth model.

A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\dfrac{\mathrm{d} P}{\mathrm{d} t} = kP(a-P),
$$

where $k > 0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a > P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t) = \dfrac{a}{1+Ce^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality $k=0.000\,01,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=10\,000.$ Therefore, the hare population is given by the equation

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d} P}{\mathrm{d} t} = 0.000\,01 P(10\,000-P) .
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
P(t) 
= \dfrac{10\,000}{1+Ce^{-(10\,000\cdot 0.000\,01)t}}= \dfrac{10\,000}{1+Ce^{-0.1t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=2\,500$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0) & =2\,500 \\ \frac{10\,000}{1+C{e}^{-0.1(0)}} & =2\,500 \\ \frac{10\,000}{1+C} & =2\,500 \\ \frac{1+C}{10\,000} & =\frac{1}{2\,500} \\ 1+C & =\frac{10\,000}{2\,500} \\ 1+C & =4 \\ C & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t) = \frac{10\,000}{1+3 e^{-0.1 t}}.
$$

Finally, to find the number of hares in the forest after $7$ years, we substitute $t=7$ into the expression for $P(t),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(7) & =\frac{10\,000}{1+3{e}^{-0.1\cdot 7}} \\  & ≈4\,016.\end{aligned}
$$
